dice/bone-dice.title: Roman bone dice from Silchester
dice/bone-dice.caption: Roman bone dice excavated at Silchester (Calleva Atrebatum), Britain.
dice/bone-dice.why: Romans gambled with bone dice (tesserae) and knucklebones (tali) — the everyday randomness behind this site's roll.

dice/delos-dice.title: Dices Roman Museum Delos ZdeDelm220
dice/delos-dice.caption: Roman-era dice from the Archaeological Museum of Delos.
dice/delos-dice.why: Delos held the Mediterranean's largest slave market — the same throw of fortune that decided a life.

titus-caecilius/lararium.commons_file: File:Lararium in the atrium of Casa del Menandro (Pompeii) (48442861451).jpg
titus-caecilius/lararium.title: Lararium in the atrium of Casa del Menandro (Pompeii) (48442861451)
titus-caecilius/lararium.caption: A household shrine (lararium), House of the Menander, Pompeii.
titus-caecilius/lararium.why: Titus worshipped the Lares at a shrine exactly like this before every planting.

titus-caecilius/farming.title: Cherchel-Mosaic-lower-register
titus-caecilius/farming.caption: Mosaic of ploughing and field labour, Cherchell (Caesarea), Roman Africa.
titus-caecilius/farming.why: Emmer wheat, oxen and the agricultural year that governed his entire life.

kalasiris/estate.commons_file: File:Dominus Julius mosaic in the Bardo National Museum(12240864473).jpg
kalasiris/estate.title: Dominus Julius mosaic in the Bardo National Museum(12240864473)
kalasiris/estate.caption: The 'Dominus Julius' mosaic, Bardo Museum, Tunis — a great estate and its labourers.
kalasiris/estate.why: The latifundium economy that consumed enslaved field-hands like Kalasiris.

kalasiris/captive.title: Roman Figurine of Bound Captive
kalasiris/captive.caption: Roman figurine of a bound captive (Portable Antiquities Scheme).
kalasiris/captive.why: Enslavement through war and raiding — how a free Bithynian boy became property.

helene/fayum.commons_file: File:Fayum mummy portrait (160-180 AD) - British museum, EA74710.jpg
helene/fayum.title: Fayum mummy portrait (160-180 AD) - British museum, EA74710
helene/fayum.caption: Fayum mummy portrait of a woman, c. 160–180 AD, British Museum.
helene/fayum.why: "The famous Fayum portraits are exactly the faces of people like you." — her own generation.

helene/sobek.commons_file: File:Statue presenting a shrine with an image of the god Sobek, graywacke - Museo Egizio Turin C 3043 p01.jpg
helene/sobek.title: Statue presenting a shrine (“naophore”) with an image of the god Sobek title QS:P1476,en:"Statue presenting a shrine (“naophore”) with an image of the god Sobek "label QS:Len,"Statue presenting a shrine (“naophore”) with an image of the god Sobek "label QS:Lit,"Statua che presenta un’edicola (“naofora”) con un’immagine di Sobek"
helene/sobek.caption: Statue with a shrine of the crocodile god Sobek, Museo Egizio, Turin.
helene/sobek.why: Sobek was the traditional god of the Fayum that Helene worshipped.

petronia-iusta/baker.commons_file: File:Fresco portrait of the baker Terentius Neo and his wife, from Pompeii.jpg
petronia-iusta/baker.title: Fresco portrait of the baker Terentius Neo and his wife, from Pompeii
petronia-iusta/baker.caption: Fresco of the baker Terentius Neo and his wife, Pompeii.
petronia-iusta/baker.why: Her father worked a bakery; this couple are the social world she came from.

petronia-iusta/lamp.title: Terracotta oil lamp
petronia-iusta/lamp.credit: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art. See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy
petronia-iusta/lamp.caption: Roman terracotta oil lamp, Metropolitan Museum of Art.
petronia-iusta/lamp.why: Petronia painted decorations on lamps exactly like this for a living.

petronia-iusta/latrine.commons_file: File:Ancient Roman Public Latrine, Ostia Antica (6075060094).jpg
petronia-iusta/latrine.title: Ancient Roman Public Latrine, Ostia Antica (6075060094)
petronia-iusta/latrine.credit: Ancient Roman Public Latrine, Ostia Antica
petronia-iusta/latrine.caption: Public latrine, Ostia Antica.
petronia-iusta/latrine.why: The shared latrine — sanitation for the urban poor who had only a chamber pot at home.

gaius-vibius-celer/caelius.commons_file: File:Cenotaph of Marcus Caelius, 1st centurion of Legio XVIII, who fell in the war of Varus (Battle in the Teutoburg Forest (9 AD), LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn (9510859222).jpg
gaius-vibius-celer/caelius.title: Cenotaph of Marcus Caelius, 1st centurion of Legio XVIII, who fell in the war of Varus (Battle in the Teutoburg Forest (9 AD), LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn (9510859222)
gaius-vibius-celer/caelius.credit:
Cenotaph of Marcus Caelius, 1st centurion of Legio XVIII, who fell in the war of Varus (Battle in the Teutoburg Forest (9 AD), LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn

Uploaded by Marcus Cyron
gaius-vibius-celer/caelius.caption: Cenotaph of Marcus Caelius, centurion of Legio XVIII, lost in the Varus disaster, LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn.
gaius-vibius-celer/caelius.why: Celer's legion XIX marched into Teutoburg; Caelius of XVIII died there. "You had known men among those bones."

gaius-vibius-celer/kalkriese-mask.title: Kalkriese mask
gaius-vibius-celer/kalkriese-mask.caption: Iron cavalry face-mask found at Kalkriese, the Teutoburg battlefield.
gaius-vibius-celer/kalkriese-mask.why: Recovered from the killing ground itself — the physical residue of the ambush of 9 AD.

gaius-vibius-celer/diploma.title: Bronze military diploma
gaius-vibius-celer/diploma.credit: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art. See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy
gaius-vibius-celer/diploma.caption: Bronze Roman military diploma, Metropolitan Museum of Art.
gaius-vibius-celer/diploma.why: On discharge Celer received a diploma like this, granting citizenship to his children.

publius-valerius-messalla/togatus.title: Togato Barberini
publius-valerius-messalla/togatus.caption: The 'Togatus Barberini' — a Roman holding busts of his ancestors (imagines).
publius-valerius-messalla/togatus.why: At Messalla's funeral the imagines of his ancestors were paraded through the Forum.

publius-valerius-messalla/arapacis.commons_file: File:Relief of the Ara Pacis Augustae with Procession-Uffizi.jpg
publius-valerius-messalla/arapacis.title: Relief of the Ara Pacis Augustae with Procession-Uffizi
publius-valerius-messalla/arapacis.caption: Processional relief from the Ara Pacis Augustae, Rome.
publius-valerius-messalla/arapacis.why: The senatorial order on display — the world of dignitas Messalla had to perform in.

successus/thermopolium.title: Thermopolium Lucius Vetutius Placidus Pompeii
successus/thermopolium.caption: Thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus, on the Via dell'Abbondanza, Pompeii.
successus/thermopolium.why: A hot-food-and-drink counter with embedded dolia on the exact street named in his story.

successus/tavern.commons_file: File:Tavern scene from VI 14, 36 (Caupona of Salvius) by Geremia Discanno pub 1882.jpg
successus/tavern.title: Tavern scene from VI 14, 36 (Caupona of Salvius) by Geremia Discanno pub 1882
successus/tavern.credit: https://archive.org/details/pompejidieneuest00pres Pompeji die neuesten Ausgrabungen von 1874 bis 1881
successus/tavern.caption: Tavern scene fresco from the Caupona of Salvius, Pompeii (19th-c. reproduction).
successus/tavern.why: Drinkers, dice and quarrels — the low-culture social world of his counter.

successus/cast.commons_file: File:Pompeii Plaster cast of a victim.jpg
successus/cast.title: Pompeii Plaster cast of a victim
successus/cast.caption: Plaster cast of a victim of the 79 AD eruption, Pompeii.
successus/cast.why: How Successus's own death was preserved: a void in the ash, filled with plaster.

boudiga/gorgon.title: 'Gorgon's Head' - Bath Temple Pediment
boudiga/gorgon.caption: The 'Gorgon's head' from the temple pediment of Sulis Minerva, Roman Baths, Bath.
boudiga/gorgon.why: Boudiga made a pilgrimage to Aquae Sulis, a day's journey from home.

boudiga/curse.commons_file: File:A metal curse tablet (defixio) with a complaint about the theft of a Vilbia.jpg
boudiga/curse.title: A metal curse tablet (defixio) with a complaint about the theft of a Vilbia
boudiga/curse.caption: A lead curse tablet (defixio) from Bath, complaining of a theft.
boudiga/curse.why: She threw a curse tablet just like this into the sacred spring over a stolen possession.

boudiga/mosaic.title: Hunting Dogs Mosaic, Corinium Museum (Cirencester) (16178671784)
boudiga/mosaic.caption: The 'Hunting Dogs' mosaic, Corinium Museum, Cirencester.
boudiga/mosaic.why: Corinium — the new Roman town that grew up beside her tribe's old territory.

aurelius-diza/mithras.title: Mithras sacrificing a bulllabel QS:Lfr,"Mithra sacrifiant le taureau"label QS:Len,"Mithras sacrificing a bull"label QS:Les,"Mitra matando al toro"label QS:Lit,"Mitra uccide il toro"label QS:Lca,"Mitra sacrificant un toro"
aurelius-diza/mithras.caption: Mithras slaying the bull (tauroctony), British Museum.
aurelius-diza/mithras.why: The mystery cult of Mithras was enormously popular among soldiers like Diza.

aurelius-diza/coin.title: Antoninianus of Gallienus - Obverse
aurelius-diza/coin.caption: Debased antoninianus of the emperor Gallienus (r. 253–268).
aurelius-diza/coin.why: Diza was paid in coins like this — by the 260s under 5% silver, nearly worthless.

aurelius-diza/tombstone.title: Tombstone of Aurel(ius) Monimus;  RIU-05, 01193 = Schober 00229 = RHP 00328 = CBI 00402 = BfIntercisa 00007 = AE 1912, 00007: D(is) M(anibus) // Aur(elio) Monimo b(ene)f(iciario) / trib(uni) coh(ortis) oo(milliariae) H/emes(enorum) stip(endiorum) XXIIII / vixit an(nos) XLV / G() Bassus lib(ertus) / b(ene) m(erenti) p(osuit) ex ipsi/us praeceptolabel QS:Len,"Tombstone of Aurel(ius) Monimus;  RIU-05, 01193 = Schober 00229 = RHP 00328 = CBI 00402 = BfIntercisa 00007 = AE 1912, 00007: D(is) M(anibus) // Aur(elio) Monimo b(ene)f(iciario) / trib(uni) coh(ortis) oo(milliariae) H/emes(enorum) stip(endiorum) XXIIII / vixit an(nos) XLV / G() Bassus lib(ertus) / b(ene) m(erenti) p(osuit) ex ipsi/us praecepto"label QS:Lhu,"Aurel(ius) Monimus sírköve"
aurelius-diza/tombstone.credit: Own work; Photo by Szilas in the Hungarian National Museum
aurelius-diza/tombstone.caption: Roman tombstone of Aurelius Monimus.
aurelius-diza/tombstone.why: Diza named his son Aurelius Mokimos; auxiliary epitaphs like this fill the Intercisa cemetery.

flavius-marcellinus/missorium.title: Disco de Teodosio
flavius-marcellinus/missorium.caption: The Missorium of Theodosius I — the emperor amid his court and officials.
flavius-marcellinus/missorium.why: The hierarchy of the late-Roman state that Marcellinus served from its lower rungs.

flavius-marcellinus/notitia.title: Notitia Dignitatum - Primicerius notariorum
flavius-marcellinus/notitia.artist: Peronet Lamy (died 1453), based on Roman originals
flavius-marcellinus/notitia.caption: Page from the Notitia Dignitatum — insignia of the chief of the notaries.
flavius-marcellinus/notitia.why: The actual register of late-Roman offices; Marcellinus worked in a records bureau like this.

flavius-marcellinus/walls.title: Theodosian Walls of Constantinople, Istanbul (24053561188)
flavius-marcellinus/walls.caption: The Theodosian Walls of Constantinople.
flavius-marcellinus/walls.why: "Constantinople was secure behind its massive walls" while the West unravelled.
